items.description: Upper River Derwent, Stonethwaite Beck and Derwent Water
items.message:
Derwent Water remains high following recent rainfall and a Flood Alert will remain in force.  Derwent Water level is currently receding and will continue to do so over the coming days as high pressure builds bringing a period of settled and dry weather.  
Locations most affected will be low lying land and roads near the Upper Derwent from Seathwaite to Derwent Water. 
We continue to closely monitor the situation. Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 9:00AM on Saturday 31 October or as the situation changes.

items.message:
There is no longer a threat of flooding.
Tidal conditions are expected to improve and no flooding is expected.  
We will continue to monitor the situation and will issue further alerts or warnings if necessary.  
Continue to take care on waterside roads and footpaths and don't put yourself in unnecessary danger.

items.description: The tidal Rivers Bure, Ant and Thurne
items.message: Higher than normal tides today may lead to flooding. Flooding is possible from 12 noon to 3pm today, Friday 30 October. We expect to see high water levels around Potter Heigham, Wroxham boat yards and Ferry Road in Horning. Levels can take several hours to peak. The weather forecast is improving, and we expect levels to start returning to normal soon. We are monitoring rainfall and river levels. Take care and avoid walking, cycling or driving through flood water. This message will be updated by 10am on Saturday 31 October or as the situation changes.
